> [!CAUTION]
> **Uninstalling HMG-API 1.1.0-rc.8 or older on NEMESIS 1.17 can brick the head unit.** A restart or two after the uninstall, Android stops starting and the screen never gets past boot. Recovering then needs a USB stick or a laptop with adb ([#397](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/issues/397)), and may not always be possible without the dealer.
>
> **This only happens when all three are true:**
> - the head unit has **NEMESIS 1.17** installed, and
> - it runs **HMG-API 1.1.0-rc.8 or older**, and
> - you **uninstall** HMG-API.
>
> **Not affected:** NEMESIS 1.16 or older, units without NEMESIS, and updating HMG-API (updating is safe).
>
> **On NEMESIS 1.17, under no circumstances uninstall HMG-API before updating it to 1.1.0-rc.9.** Update first, then uninstall if you want to.

**HMG-API 1.1.0-rc.9 is the ninth release candidate, with fixes for HMG-API under NEMESIS 1.17.** NEMESIS 1.17's LivePatch takes over the file Android starts from (`/system/bin/app_process`). Earlier HMG-API releases didn't know that, so on NEMESIS 1.17 **uninstalling them could leave the head unit unable to start Android** a couple of restarts later. This RC fixes that. 1.1.0 will be this code unless a blocker turns up. **This RC hasn't been checked on a car yet**, so please report how it goes. If you'd rather wait, stay on [1.0.2](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/releases/tag/v1.0.2), but don't uninstall it on NEMESIS 1.17 (below).

It comes with the same mods as rc.8: **Wireless CarPlay + Android Auto [2.2.0-rc.9](https://github.com/Open-HMG/hmgapi-wireless-cp-aa/releases/tag/v2.2.0-rc.9)**, **ADB [1.0.1-rc.1](https://github.com/Open-HMG/hmgapi-adb/releases/tag/v1.0.1-rc.1)**, and NEMESIS in the app menu.

## On NEMESIS 1.17: update before you uninstall

The uninstall that runs is the one saved when HMG-API was installed. On NEMESIS 1.17, **update to this RC first, then uninstall** if you want to. Don't uninstall 1.1.0-rc.8 or older there.

**If you already uninstalled an older HMG-API on NEMESIS 1.17:** the first restart after it works, and the one after that doesn't start Android.
- **The head unit hasn't restarted since you uninstalled:** install this RC as new now (`hmgapi-1.1.0-rc.9-usb.zip`, or the NEMESIS package). That fixes it, whichever version you uninstalled.
- **It has restarted once and Android still runs:** if you uninstalled without `--purge`, install this RC now, whichever version it was. It puts the missing stock file back from HMG-API's backup. If you used `--purge`, the backup is gone, and this RC's install refuses and changes nothing. Follow [#397](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/issues/397) instead.
- **Android already doesn't start:** follow [#397](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/issues/397). A NEMESIS USB stick puts the stock file back with no PC needed, as long as you didn't uninstall with `--purge`.

## What's new since 1.1.0-rc.8

- **HMG-API works under NEMESIS 1.17's LivePatch** (#396, by @zpoon; @isaacwisdom found the case of an older update). NEMESIS 1.17 puts its own script at `app_process` and starts Android from `app_process.real`. HMG-API now installs into `app_process.real` and leaves NEMESIS's script alone, and the uninstall puts the stock file back there. Before, on NEMESIS 1.17:
  - uninstalling could leave Android unable to start (above);
  - updating HMG-API didn't update its zygote wrapper (the old one kept running);
  - installing HMG-API after NEMESIS 1.17 was refused ("isn't a known stock build").
- **An install no longer reports "installed" over a wrapper whose stock copy is gone** (#399, #400, by @zpoon). That's what an older uninstall leaves on NEMESIS 1.17 after a restart. The install recognises any HMG-API version's wrapper. It puts the copy back from HMG-API's stock backup when there is one, and refuses otherwise, even with `HMGAPI/FORCE`.
- **After a head-unit factory reset** (which wipes HMG-API's backups but leaves HMG-API in place), installing again takes the stock backup from HMG-API's stock copy (#400). Before, a reinstall could save the wrapper as the "stock" backup, so later uninstalls refused. Forcing the install could write the wrapper over the stock copy, so Android couldn't start. This applies with or without NEMESIS.
- Otherwise the install and uninstall work as before.
- The full list is in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/blob/v1.1.0-rc.9/CHANGELOG.md).

## Installing

- **From 1.0.x, the beta or an earlier RC:** put `hmgapi-1.1.0-rc.9-update.zip` in `HMGAPI/updates/` on a USB stick, then HMG-API app → **Check USB updates**. Restart the head unit once afterwards. Your mods and settings stay. The mods are the same as in rc.8, so there's nothing else to update if you're on rc.8.
- **With NEMESIS:** unzip `hmgapi-1.1.0-rc.9-nemesis.zip` onto a stick and update from NEMESIS Manager's Package Store.
- **New install, or after a firmware update:** follow [Installing HMG-API](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/wiki/Installing-HMG-API), with `hmgapi-1.1.0-rc.9-usb.zip`.

## What to test

- **On NEMESIS 1.17 especially:** update or install, then restart **twice**. The app shows **1.1.0-rc.9** and "Hooks on", and your mods run. If you can, uninstall, restart twice, and check that Android still starts. Then install again.
- **Without NEMESIS 1.17:** the same update, a restart, and your mods still running.
- `/data/hmgapi/install.log` says which file HMG-API used (`app_process.real` under NEMESIS 1.17). Attach it, or use **Record a problem**.

## Known issues

- Bluetooth Audio can take audio focus at a cold start before CarPlay or Android Auto is up. A fix is in review (wireless #56).
- The rest are the same as in [1.0.0](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/releases/tag/v1.0.0). For example, a USB stick left in the port can start wired Android Auto and stop wireless from connecting, so take the stick out after installing.

## Going back to 1.0.2

**Not on NEMESIS 1.17:** 1.0.2's installer and uninstaller don't know LivePatch, and its uninstall there can leave Android unable to start.

Otherwise, [1.0.2](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/releases/tag/v1.0.2) is the release to go back to. The app won't install an older HMG-API over a newer one, so either:
- **With adb:** `adb push hmgapi-1.0.2-update.zip /data/local/tmp/`, then `adb shell hmgapid engine update-hmgapi /data/local/tmp/hmgapi-1.0.2-update.zip --force`. Restart the head unit.
- **Without adb:** uninstall HMG-API ([Uninstalling](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/wiki/Uninstalling), without `PURGE`, so your mods and settings stay), restart, then install 1.0.2 as new.

Wireless 2.2.0-rc.9 needs HMG-API 1.1.0-rc.8 or newer, so going back to 1.0.2 means going back to wireless 2.1.0 too: remove the mod in the app and apply, then install `wireless-carplay-aa-2.1.0.zip` from 1.0.2's release with Check USB updates.

## Reporting

Open an [issue](https://github.com/Open-HMG/HMG-API/issues/new/choose) with your car, its head unit software (e.g. 260507), the HMG-API version, your NEMESIS version and your mods, and a Car Report if you can.
